lines.en: : I’m going to be frank with you, Arakawa. Never in a million years did I think you were going to remember this place — let alone take me here of your volition.
: Yeah, well...you said it was one of your favorite spots and today is all about you. I can be surprising every once in a while.
: I suppose you can. Color me impressed. So long as that color is black, of course.
Wakana seemed rather skeptical when I insisted that we make our way to the train station, but she more or less figured out where we were going once we got off at the Urban District.
So yeah, I guess you can say this is me finally being a good Samaritan- especially when it’s the second time today that I’ve done something positive without asking for anything in return.
I imagine most people would just call that something along the lines of “being a good friend,” and to that I’d agree. But here’s the thing — that’s normally not me.
I only vaguely remembered where this place was and needed assistance along the final stretch. And even then, I didn’t recognize the shop at first glance.
Once we set foot inside, though, it all came rushing back. Which is why I can tell you we’re sitting at the same table we were the first time we came here.
I’m sure this is where she sits with Osako as well. And I’m sure that’s who she’d rather be sitting with at this very moment.
But she’s stuck with me...so I at least owe her a dinner she can stomach in an atmosphere she loves.
And even if I feel out of place, it’s worth it just to see her smile.
: Ever think of changing your look up? Maybe trying on something that isn’t black?
: I have that grey jacket I wear to work. Does that not suffice?
: Grey is just light black.
: I’ve always looked at it as more of a dark white.
: Either way, I’m talking about light colors. Maybe a nice pink or red.
: Sorry, are you a fashion designer now? Because, if you are, I believe you may need to head back to school to learn a thing or two about color matching.
: I think those colors would look just fine on you. I think anything would look fine on you, really. You’re a beautiful girl.
: Woman, Arakawa. I am a beautiful woman. The miniature devils I teach are girls.
: Some of those miniature devils are taller than you.
: Yes, but that does naught to fix their elegance for I meant miniature in aura, not height.
: Damn. Guess I’ll just have to throw away the bright yellow dress I bought you for your birthday then.
: Oh, please. I doubt you even know when my birthday is.
: No. But if I had to take a guess, I’d imagine it’s just Halloween or something equally fitting.
: Close enough. October 10th.
: Oh, so right around the corner.
: But not so soon that you don’t have time to exchange your hypothetical dress for something more befitting a goth queen.
: Do you actually want a birthday present?
: Would you actually buy me one if I did?
: Depends. Will you buy me one for mine?
: Depends on if I remember. When is it?
: It’s-
: Do you...not remember your own birthday?
: I...don’t think I do.
: Just...look at your ID, Arakawa.
: I don’t keep it on me.
: What? What if you’re stopped by the police?
: I guess I’m going to jail.
: I mean, knowing you, you’d be very likely going to jail regardless. But having your ID on you would at least save some time and-
: You know what? Forget the ID and forget my birthday. I’m buying you a present. What do you want?
: Someone else to talk to at work would be nice.
: So a set of walkie-talkies for you, Imani, and Rika. Got it.
: Arakawa.
: Please don’t lecture me. I’ve been so good today.
: You have, which is why I’m going to be as gentle as I possibly can.
: Either you come back to school by the end of the year, or I butcher you and bury you in your own backyard.
: That’s as gentle as you can be?

: I’m a very violent woman when I’m not in crippling pain. And while I understand that you may have personal issues you need to sort out, I imagine an entire school year should suffice. Should it not?
: Ara-
: It just has to be by the end of the school year?
: If you want to keep your life, yes.
: And if I don’t?
: Then I will lace your drink with cyanide and kill you now so I don’t have to worry about you anymore.
: You’d have your work cut out for you having to carry me from here all the way to my backyard.
: Which is why you should be a dear and just do as you’re told. Love, Wakana Watabe.
: Did you just end a sentence like you’d end a letter?
: PS: Fuck you.
: You really want me back there, don’t you?
: Complaining to the other girls just isn’t as fun.
: I thought you were women?
: Can you look away for a moment? And also slide your drink a tad closer to me?
I manage to get off easy concerning Wakana’s ultimatum.
Of course I have no problem agreeing to come back by the end of the school year when I know the school year won’t ever end.
But it’s not like I can just say that since if she doesn’t interrupt me, she’ll push forward the date instead.
So I keep up the pattern-
: Fine.
Make a promise I have no intention of keeping-
: I’ll come back by the end of the school year.
And narrowly avoid a sin by convincing myself that hiding the truth from someone is different from lying.
: Good boy.
: And now to drink myself into a stupor in hopes that I’ll be able to make it home without you carrying me.
: You drink as well, Arakawa. It’s on me. A reward for your rare and repeated excellence today.
: Wakana...can I ask you something now?
: Hm?
: It’s kind of...random, though.
: You’re not going to crawl into my lap like I did yours, are you? Because this is hardly the place for that.
: Can you tell me about your childhood?
: My childhood? May I at least ask what spurred such curiosity?
: It’s just that...
: I kind of block mine out. And there are certain things that remind me of it that make me want to know if others are-
: Say no more.
: It all started when I was in elementary school.
: That’s when it started?
: Is there a problem with that?
: It’s just that...most people’s lives normally start before then.
: Yes, well, you don’t want to sit here for hours as I feverishly recant the memories of my back being cut open and meticulously fiddled with, do you?
: You were awake for all that?
: No, I- ugh. Can I just start where I intended to start? Or would you prefer I begin writing my memoirs early for the sole purpose of appeasing you?
: Start wherever you want. I’ll stop getting in the way.
: I just want to know if you were happy back then.
: I can’t quite remember...but I don’t imagine I was.
: I’ve been rather “gloomy” my whole life, you see. And I imagine it was for that reason no one ever paid much attention to me.
: I imagine the Sakakibara girl from your former class would be an apt comparison. But she seems to have found her footing and begun to associate with others in a way I never really did.
: There were those who tried to tease me for the way I dressed...the things I read and wrote...but they gave up and left once they realized it didn’t particularly bother me.
: Were you just...too focused on something else back then?
: I believe it would be more accurate to say I just...wasn’t focused on anything?

: I was assuredly an outcast. But I believe at least half of that was due to an overwhelming disinterest in practically everything — with the second half being my inability to physically act as others my age did.
: I was, by all accounts, the “weird” girl. But I was one who was mostly left to her own devices so...perhaps that is why I blossomed into the poetic genius you see before you today.
: You don’t have any pictures you can show me, do you?
: Of course not. Who just carries around pictures of their younger self all day?
: Well...you’re all on social media, aren’t you? You don’t have anything there?
: Every picture I have ever posted has been a flower. If anyone would like to see my face, they are free to do so in real life.
: You know, maybe you weren’t just the “weird girl” back then because you kept to yourself. Maybe you’re just...genuinely weird.
: Maybe. For it was all the same throughout high school and most of college as well.
: But again, that never bothered me. People are just...irritating. Especially when they’re that young.
: They’re always whining about a need to “connect” with someone...and how it’s so hard to find people who actually “understand” them.
: But when their entire evaluation of a person is decided within the first ten seconds of meeting them, of course they’re not going to be understood. Connections take time.

: Those sorts of relationships where everything just clicks right away without any effort on anyone’s end just...don’t exist. They’re all made up. Mostly by terrible writers looking to cash in on romance.
: Or...at least that’s what I thought.
: Next — Osako Osaka, reading “To the River” by Edgar Allan Poe.
: Mm?
: Uhh...hi...
: That part’s...not in the poem...
: Just...
: Hahahaha! Classic Osako! Awkward as always!
: You got this, Osako! Just do it like you did in the locker room!
: Miss Osaka...if you’re unprepared for the assignment, please just say so instead of wasting everyone’s time.
: I can do it! I can do it.
: Then put the notebook down...
: Can I just...hold onto it for comfort, please? I promise I won’t look.
: No. If you’re unwilling to do the assignment as instructed-
: Aaah! Fine!
: Fair river! in thy bright, clear flow...Of crystal, wandering water...Thou art an emblem of the glow...Of beauty—the unhidden heart...The playful maziness of art...In old Alberto’s daughter...
: B-But when within thy wave she looks...Which glistens then, and trembles...Why, then, the prettiest of brooks...Her worshipper resembles...
: For in my heart, as in thy stream...Her image deeply lies...His heart which trembles at the beam...Of her soul-searching eyes...
: Is she looking at somebody? Why’s she still just standing there?
: Watabe, probably. She’s always looking at her. Have you seriously never noticed before?
: What? Really? The creepy girl? Why? They’re totally different types.
: Miss Osaka, well done. But if that will be all...please take your seat.
: S...Sorry! Bye!
: Perhaps there is some truth to immediately knowing whether or not you’ll “click” with a person...
: Because from that point on, my life has been full of color thanks to a bashful, yet sensitive jock with a secret affinity for sage and lace. And if I could go back and do it all again, I would.
: They can cut me open as many times as they want and I’ll keep looking forward to it because I know what lies ahead. And it’s something unlike anything else in the world.
: I apologize if that wasn’t the sort of nostalgic retelling you were hoping for, Arakawa. I have no traumatic tale of neglect or abuse or anything else you could have hopefully connected with.
: But I hope with this shriveled, blackened heart of mine that, one day, you will have a moment like I did — where you see someone or something for the first time and think “this is why I’m here.”
: Perhaps you already have and simply haven’t told me. There is that childhood friend of yours, after all. And many others too.
: I’m not looking to know everything — just what you’re willing to share.
: And I may not have enough happiness for the two of us right now...
: But if I ever do, I hope you’ll take some of it off my hands.
: I can only smile for so long until my face begins to hurt.
: Maybe one day.
: Maybe, indeed.
Wakana and I finish our respective meals before she takes out her phone and begins to scroll through every photo she has ever posted to social media.
Each one is just as she said — a flower.
But there’s only one that brings me hope. Or joy, if you could call it that.
I ask her if she’ll send it to me and she smiles.
Then, we take the train back to the first half of town.
I carry her for the last block on the way to her apartment, but I probably didn’t have to.
When we get to her door, I exercise a brand new right of mine.
I imagine it will happen again.
Then, I gaze at that photo all the way home.
It isn’t why I’m here.
But it’s close.
I can feel it.
Wakana’s affection has increased to [wakana_love]!
